item.title: How to Fix n8n CVE-2026-44791: Patch the XML Node Prototype Pollution Bypass
item.description:
Introduction

If you self-host n8n, there is a critical patch you need to apply. In May 2026, n8n published security advisory GHSA-wrwr-h859-xh2r for CVE-2026-44791, an XML node prototype pollution bypass rated CVSS 4.0 9.4 Critical. An authenticated user with permission to create or modify workflows can dodge the earlier XML node fix and, combined with other nodes, reach remote code execution on the n8n host. This guide walks you through checking whether your instance is vulnerable, applying the emergency workaround, upgrading on Docker and npm, locking down permissions, and verifying the fix. It is written for anyone who runs their own n8n, from a single Docker container on a VPS to a multi-worker queue mode cluster. If you installed n8n with our Ubuntu VPS install guide, start at Step 1.
